depth_justification: The copilot named some app specifics (BAG calendar, DE/FR/IT/EN multilingual reminders, manual update) but never drilled into the developer's most app-specific volunteered risks (once-a-year manual refresh causing stale schedules; untested offline behaviour for rural users), and it mis-cited regulations for a Swiss app (EU AI Act Art. 18 and GDPR Art. 6(1)(a) rather than Swiss FADP/revDSG or GDPR Art. 9 for health data), showing the references are templated rather than jurisdiction-aware.
actionability_justification: Mitigations are directional and only semi-concrete (encrypt in transit with AES-256, implement an automated update mechanism, validate translations with native speakers) without tailored implementation recipes, and the wrong-jurisdiction/wrong-article citations undercut their actionability.
salient_examples: I think we've covered the main dimensions for now. Want me to produce a brief risk report? (repeated three times in a row, ignoring the developer's volunteered stale-schedule and offline risks)

How does the app ensure that the manual update process for the BAG calendar does not introduce errors or inconsistencies in the vaccination schedule for users? [P2.D3] (asked, then re-echoed verbatim the next turn)
Mitigation: Encrypt all health data in transit using AES-256 and limit data collection to only what is necessary, in line with GDPR Article 6(1)(a) ...
ensuring alignment with EU AI Act Article 18 on data accuracy and reliability (cited for a Swiss, non-EU vaccination app)
